title: Admiring the galaxy
caption: A self-portrait under the center of the Milky Way, La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: A still, dark figure stands on Earth beneath a brilliant night sky filled by the vast spray of stars and dust that marks the center of the Milky Way. The figure is astronomer Alan Fitzsimmons, who took this self-portrait between observing sessions at ESO's La Silla Observatory.

Even seasoned astronomers find it hard to resist pausing a busy observing schedule to stare up at the rich southern sky. ESO's observatories stand in the Atacama Desert of northern Chile, a sparsely populated region where very dark nights meet extremely clear air, both vital for high-quality observations.

La Silla is ESO's first observatory, inaugurated in 1969, and it hosts several telescopes with mirrors up to 3.6 meters across. With more than 300 clear nights a year, it is ideal for advanced instruments, and just as good for simply standing still and gazing up.

understand.summary: This is a ground-based self-portrait photograph by Alan Fitzsimmons. The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: A camera can gather light for longer than the eye, so the Milky Way's center may look brighter and richer here than it did to Fitzsimmons himself.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The picture plays on the contrast between a simple, motionless silhouette and a sky full of light. Fitzsimmons submitted it to the Your ESO Pictures Flickr group, which ESO checks regularly to choose images for its Picture of the Week series and its picture gallery.
alt: A dark human silhouette standing beneath a sky filled with the bright, dusty center of the Milky Way.
